title: 8 ways that U.S.-style democracy stands out globally
summary: As the U.S. celebrates the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence this year, here are eight ways its political system stands apart from the world's other 105 democracies.

title: Majority of Americans support banning social media for kids under 16
summary: Across major demographic and partisan groups, more Americans support than oppose banning those under 16 from using social media.

title: 5% of Americans say they’ve ridden in a driverless car
summary: Regardless of whether they’ve ridden in one before, most Americans (71%) say they would be not too or not at all comfortable riding in a driverless car.

title: About a third of U.S. Democrats like political leaders who identify as democratic socialists
summary: Democrats’ views on democratic socialists also differ by race and ethnicity, age, education, income and political engagement.

title: 5 facts about religion in the Philippines
summary: Nearly all Filipinos believe in God, most pray daily and 92% identify as Christian, with Catholics as the majority.

title: Which Americans are most likely to have spoken with a local journalist?
summary: About a quarter of Americans have spoken with a local journalist, with education, income, race and community attachment linked to higher rates of interaction.

title: Buying a home has gotten harder for young adults in most U.S. metro areas
summary: About nine-in-ten adults under 40 say buying a home is harder than it was for their parents, as rising prices and mortgage rates push homeownership further out of reach.

title: More than half of states restrict betting on elections
summary: Lawmakers in at least 16 states have introduced legislation this year to regulate prediction markets in some way.

title: What happens when war breaks out in the middle of a survey?
summary: Using statistical analysis of surveys fielded during the U.S.-Israel airstrikes on Iran, researchers tracked real-time shifts in global views of the U.S. and national economies.

title: Trump Gets Negative Reviews Internationally as Fewer Say U.S. Is a Reliable Partner
summary: A 36-country survey finds declining ratings for the U.S. amid rising concerns about its foreign policy and the health of its democracy.

title: How do views of Trump compare with other global leaders?
summary: Of the six leaders asked about, only Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu ranks below President Donald Trump in confidence.

title: Comparing how Americans and others around the world view the United States’ global role
summary: Majorities in most countries say the U.S. does not promote peace and stability or consider other countries’ interests on policy matters.

title: European views of Trump and the U.S. are especially negative
summary: Views of the U.S. and its president are negative across the globe, but Europeans stand out for their especially unfavorable views.

title: In middle-income nations, most say the U.S. interferes in other countries’ affairs
summary: Majorities in 16 of 17 middle-income nations say this, including roughly three-quarters of adults or more in 12 countries.

title: Many Americans favor prayer in public schools, but few think it should be mandatory
summary: Americans are almost equally split on whether the Ten Commandments should be displayed in public school classrooms. But Republicans, White evangelicals and older Americans are more supportive than other groups.

title: Catholics in Latin America generally have positive views of Pope Leo
summary: In six Latin American countries surveyed, most Catholics view Pope Leo XIV favorably, though his ratings trail those Pope Francis received early in his papacy.

title: Most U.S. Catholics view Pope Leo favorably; many think Trump has been too critical of him
summary: About eight-in-ten U.S. Catholics view Pope Leo XIV favorably, though opinions on the tension between Leo and President Trump split sharply along party lines.

title: Is U.S. fertility at an all-time low? It depends how you measure it
summary: U.S. fertility rates have hit historic lows, but three common measures tell different stories about whether American families are truly shrinking.

title: What the data says about abortion in the U.S.
summary: Six-in-ten US adults say abortion should be legal in all or most cases. Here's a look at data on abortion rates, providers, demographics and more.

title: Americans and AI 2026: Chatbots, Smart Devices and Views on Impact
summary: More Americans are using chatbots, and some are adopting AI summaries and smart speakers. But views about AI and how fast it’s advancing tilt negative – even for younger adults.

summary: The existence of artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from a question of if to when, and now. title: Why don’t people use chatbots?
summary: Although chatbot use is rising in the United States, about half of U.S. adults say they never use one, according to Pew Research Center’s February survey of U.S. adults. title: How opinions and use of AI differ by age
summary: For decades, age has been a key factor in Americans’ technology use, and artificial intelligence (AI) is no exception. In February, Pew Research Center surveyed over 5,000 U.S. adults to understand how that story is playing out today. Among the takeaways: While most adults under 30 use chatbots, they’re the most skeptical about AI’s future […]

title: The gender gap in AI
summary: Does gender factor into how people use and think about artificial intelligence (AI)? In some ways, it does. Men report using chatbots more regularly than women and are more likely to turn to them for a variety of things, including work.
